To approve the closure
of Barnard Castle Register Office after all existing ceremony
bookings conclude in December 2026; to cease taking new bookings
beyond the closure date; to serve the required three months’
notice on Barnard Castle and Eden Auction Mart Company by the end
of September 2026; and to progress the associated dilapidations,
repair, cleaning and communications actions.
 
Options considered:
(1) retain and refurbish the existing leased premises; (2)
reinstate registration appointments at the existing office; (3)
provide a registration service from an alternative Barnard Castle
venue, including the library or another local location; and (4)
close the office and continue to provide Registration Services from
The Story, while honouring existing Barnard Castle ceremony
bookings.
 
Reasons: The office
currently provides ceremony space only. Registration appointments
ceased in 2019/20. Over the last three financial years, 41
ceremonies were held at the office. The premises cost approximately
£18,000 each year to run, including £6,000 rent, and
require approximately £4,000 of internal refurbishment. A
targeted consultation between 2 and 30 April 2026 identified
concerns about accessibility, travel and loss of local provision.
These representations were considered alongside service capacity
and resilience, secure certificate-storage requirements, financial
implications and the introduction of telephone death registration
from September 2026. The demand and income generated do not justify
retaining or refurbishing the premises, and alternative local
registration provision would reduce appointment capacity and
service resilience at The Story. Existing 2026 ceremonies will be
honoured.

To approve Durham County Council entering into
a Property Management Agreement with Savills UK Limited for The
Newgate Centre, Bishop Auckland, and to authorise the appropriate
officer(s)
to execute the agreement on behalf of the
Council. The agreement formalises Savills UK Limited as property
manager with effect from 1 June 2026 for a term of 12 months. The
principal fees are a management fee of £28,000 per annum,
£150 per lease per annum for rent collection, and an
£8,000 set-up fee. The agreement may be terminated by giving
three months’ written notice.
 
Options considered: The report records that a
replacement property manager was required following termination of
the previous manager’s appointment with effect from 31 May
2026. An internal procurement process was completed and Savills UK
Limited was selected as the preferred provider. The decision is
therefore to formalise the appointment through execution of the
Property Management
Agreement.
 
Reasons: Savills UK Limited commenced property
management services on 1 June 2026, ensuring continuity of
management. The agreement provides the contractual framework for
day-to-day management, tenant and contractor liaison, service
charge administration, and oversight of the operation and upkeep of
the Centre. Savills UK Limited is also acting as the
Council’s agent for the proposed disposal, providing
continuity of property knowledge and supporting due diligence and
purchaser handover. Durham County Council Legal Services reviewed
and approved the proposed agreement, and the report confirms that
the relevant procurement process and internal approvals were
completed.

content:
Durham
County Council Archaeology Section annually prepares and updates a
Standards document to reflect changes in heritage practice, new
techniques, or changes in policy and/or legislation. Our standards
are drawn from both national policy and legislation, and also a
range of professional standards from national heritage and
archaeological bodies. They are prepared to ensure that
archaeological work undertaken within the county is carried out to
a consistent, transparent, and professional standard. These
Standards aid in promoting and safeguarding the historic
environment in our region, and ensure
that the knowledge gained through collaborative archaeological
investigation is available for the benefit of the residents of
County Durham and Darlington, and the wider community. All persons,
companies and/or institutions carrying our archaeological works in
the county will apply and abide by these standards. Durham County
Council Archaeology Section will monitor compliance through normal
business procedures. This decision is to approve the latest version
of the Standards Document
topline: The Head of Environment has decided to approve the latest version of the Standards Document for archaeological work in County Durham.

content:
A decision was required on whether to replace the
existing disc-based PACE

interview-recording process with a PACE-compliant
digital system.

 

Options considered included retaining the current
physical-media workflow or

adopting the new digital recording
software.

 

Retaining the existing process would maintain
familiar practices but would continue

to present operational inefficiencies and reliance
on outdated hardware. The digital

option was selected as testing confirmed that it
meets PACE Code E requirements,

provides secure and tamper-evident recordings
through checksum validation, and

offers clear operational and evidential
benefits.

 

This option was chosen as it modernises the
recording process, improves efficiency,
and maintains evidential
integrity without introducing any unacceptable risks.
topline: The Corporate Director of Regeneration and Local Services has decided to replace the existing disc-based PACE interview-recording process with a PACE-compliant digital system.

content:
MITIE PFI exited the
Pension Fund in a surplus position and have made representations
that the surplus should be paid to them as an Exit Credit
payment.
 
Darlington Borough
Council (as the original employer that the MITE PFI staff
transferred from) made representations that the surplus should
remain in the Fund, as MITIE PFI were only in surplus because
assets had notionally transferred to them from Darlington Borough
Council to ensure MITIE PFI were set up as ‘fully
funded’ at the outset of the admission, despite the fact
Darlington Borough Council was significantly underfunded at that
time.
 
The Pension Fund
actuary provided information that showed the impact of that initial
funding decision would be worth around four times the size of the
potential exit credit payment.
 
Consequently, on this
basis, and also because neither employer had any expectation that
an exit credit payment could be made when the admission started in
2006, the determination is that no exit credit is paid to MITIE PFI
following their exit from the Fund.
topline: The Corporate Director of Resources has decided that no exit credit will be paid to MITIE PFI following their exit from the Pension Fund.

abutments and pointing the abutments as necessary.

completed.
